title: What Is Microdosing? - Mind Mend
abstract:
The term “microdosing” means consuming very small doses of psilocybin. It’s a long-term practice among psychedelic lovers that dates back centuries.  
Featured Image:  
**magic mushrooms helps people get the health benefits of LSD and psilocybin**[Microdosing](https://www.mindmend.co/faqs/)*without*the hallucinogenic effects.Before offering psilocybin as a microdose, one must reduce its psychedelic effects to a specific level. It should be low enough for you to comfortably go about your everyday activities.Psychedelic microdosing helps many people start their day and stay active throughout. Apart from its cognitive and somatic benefits, microdosing LSD is the best way to start psilocybin consumption — specifically for new users.Taking such tiny amounts will help you gauge psilocybin’s side effects. Then, you can make an informed decision on your dose and frequency moving forward.

## Dosing Guide  
### Microdose (0.05 – 0.25 Milligrams)  
A microdose is sub-perceptual, with no drastic visual effects. But this doesn’t mean this level of microdosing doesn’t pack a positive punch.With a microdose, our shrooms are working hard behind the scenes to boost your:  
- Mood
- Energy
- Focus
- Performance
- Senses
## Benefits of Microdosing  
### Mental Health  
People commonly turn to microdosing psychedelics for their mental health. Several studies confirm this.In fact, in one study in**researchers learned,**[Psychopharmacology](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00213-020-05477-0)  
> About 9% of the respondents revealed they used microdosing to help with other mental health illnesses, and 44% of them perceived their mental health to be way better after microdosing psychedelics.Another study in*21% of people revealed they primarily used microdosing as a therapy for depression. While 7% used microdosing for symptoms of anxiety.”*  
**used an online questionnaire to gauge the effects of microdosing versus typical treatments for depression and anxiety.It turns out people consider microdosing to be more effective than some other treatments. However, it seemed to be less effective than higher doses of psychedelics.The studies just get more specific.In one**[Frontiers in Psychiatry](https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fpsyt.2019.00672/full)**researchers noted microdosing the psychedelic Dimethyltryptamine (DMT) helped to alleviate anxiety in rats.
